images.filename: File-Photograph of rockfall. Rockfalls occurs naturally along the West Mesa escarpment and have the potential-to destroy petroglyphs (d1e05cf9-912b-4e25-9659-deda0cfb1d6d).JPG
images.caption:
Photograph of rockfall. Rockfalls occurs naturally along the West Mesa escarpment and have the potential
to destroy petroglyphs or create safety hazards for visitors. In early 2005, a visitor mishap in the Boca Negra area of
the monument caused the large boulder shown in the photograph to tumble down onto the steps. A pickup truck

was stranded about 8 m (25 ft) up the escarpment; the boulder was dislodged when the truck was removed
images.alt:

images.caption: composite photo of the October 14, 2023 Annular Eclipse showing full annularity and the sun before and after full annularity. As seen from Petroglyph National Monument in New Mexico, United States. The times of the photos are: 10:29:05, 10:31:38, 10:34:11, 10:36:44 (maximum annularity), 10:39:17, 10,41:50, and 10:44:23. The camera was in a fixed position so the images of the sun show their actual relative position to each other.

images.filename: Bird Motif in Boca Negra Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
images.caption: This bird, according to archeologists, is created in the Rio Grande style, which developed around 1300 AD by ancestors of the modern Pueblo people.
images.alt: This bird, according to archeologists, is created in the Rio Grande style, which developed around 1300 AD by ancestors of the modern Pueblo people.

images.caption: Although some images created on the volcanic rocks may seem recognizable, some archeologists are hesitant to interpret their meaning.
images.alt: Although some images created on the volcanic rocks may seem recognizable, some archeologists are hesitant to interpret their meaning.

images.filename: Century-old Petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
images.caption: Although most of the petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon were made by Ancestral Puebloans about 400-700 years ago, there was also evidence of Spanish engagement. Here some people left their own marks about one hundred years ago.
images.alt: Although most of the petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon were made by Ancestral Puebloans about 400-700 years ago, there was also evidence of Spanish engagement. Here some people left their own marks about one hundred years ago.

images.filename: Animal Images in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
images.caption: In the sixteenth century, both Spanish explorers and Mexicans came to the Rio Grande area and left evidence of their existence. In the late seventeenth century, parts of the West Mesa were associated with the Atrisco Land Grant which was awarded to colonists by the Spanish crown, and these colonists made their marks on the rocks.
images.alt: In the sixteenth century, both Spanish explorers and Mexicans came to the Rio Grande area and left evidence of their existence. In the late seventeenth century, parts of the West Mesa were associated with the Atrisco Land Grant which was awarded to colonists by the Spanish crown, and these colonists made their marks on the rocks.

images.filename: Old Petroglyphs in Rinconada Canyon at Petroglyph National Monument.jpg
images.caption: Although most of the images in Rinconada Canyon are believed to be about 400-700 years old, some petroglyphs could be thousands of years old. It is difficult to see all 1,200 images in the canyon.
images.alt: Although most of the images in Rinconada Canyon are believed to be about 400-700 years old, some petroglyphs could be thousands of years old. It is difficult to see all 1,200 images in the canyon.
